newsitem.title: USA: PC stocks post 2nd day of gains on Compaq report.
newsitem.headline: PC stocks post 2nd day of gains on Compaq report.

text.p: Leading personal computer maker stocks sizzled Thursday as investors followed through on a second day of buying after Compaq Computer Corp's strong quarterly results and upbeat outlook for 1997.

Analysts said Dell Computer Corp was the secondary beneficiary of investor enthusiasm, sparked by Compaq's performance, especially sales to corporate customers. Dell rose 3-1/2 to 70-1/4 amid a spree of technology buying.
Gateway 2000 Inc also captured a share of the limelight, rising 1-3/4 to 64-3/8, part of a string of gains that have pushed the stock up $10 over the past week.
By late afternoon, Compaq had gained $3 to 86-3/8, part of a two-day jump of nearly nine points.

"Dell is mostly focused on the corporate market, so people are drawing the analogy," said Goldman analyst Richard Schutte. "We saw a solid quarter from Compaq and a solid outlook" of Compaq's fourth quarter results and 1997 forecast.
"I think it's clear Compaq had good strong corporate sales, even if retail was not as strong," Schutte added.
"People understand that corporate PC buying cycles are stronger than ever," Southwest Securities analyst Gene Ramirez said. "They are expecting Dell to beat the numbers as well.
"We are seeing that factored into the stocks of Dell and Gateway," he said. Ramirez rated Dell a strong buy, Compaq a buy. He does not directly cover Gateway.
"Everyone has probably gone through their models and said, "Well, if Compaq can do it, then Dell can too," agreed Soundview Financial Group analyst Mark Specker.

But he noted how a competitive cloud looms on Dell's horizon: Compaq is expected on Friday to introduce a plan to allow some of its distribution partners to take over some parts of the final PC assembly process.
Specker said Compaq's plan would graft some of the features of Dell's high-growth direct sales and distribution model onto Compaq's traditionally indirect approach.
"There is likely to be some information that comes out tomorrow that decreases the difference between the two companies's business models," Specker said.
